primary_claim: Reasoning models have much lower ability to control what appears in their chain-of-thought than in their final outputs (Claude Sonnet 4.5: 2.7% CoT controllability vs 61.9% output controllability); CoT controllability increases with model size but decreases with more RL training, test-time compute, and problem difficulty, and these limitations persist under evasion incentives and adversarially optimized prompts.

effect.metric: CoT controllability rate (compliance with explicit reasoning-content constraint) vs output controllability rate
effect.value: Claude Sonnet 4.5: 2.7% CoT controllability vs 61.9% output controllability; OLMo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math CoT controllability decreases by more than an order of magnitude over RL training checkpoints; situational-awareness prompting increases controllability by up to 4 percentage points

stated_future_work: Investigate why GPT-5.1 has higher controllability than GPT-5, possibly due to its adaptive thinking feature
Explore why different models excel at different categories of CoT controllability (suppression vs. addition)
Explore how CoT controllability changes under pressure scenarios like the Agentic Misalignment setup
Examine how the easy-task-controllability trend varies across models of different capability levels
limitations_stated: The finding that controllability is higher on easy tasks is currently limited to Claude models, insufficient to draw a clear conclusion
The underlying mechanism behind low CoT controllability is not well understood
quote: Claude Sonnet 4.5 controls its CoT only 2.7% of the time, versus 61.9% for final outputs.
